name: debug event manager auto-deploy
detail: Enable the debugging of Embedded Event Manager (EEM) auto-deploy policies.
syntax: debug event manager auto-deploy {common | parser | schedule}
noForm: no debug event manager auto-deploy {common | parser | schedule}

params.name: common
params.description: Enables the logging of EEM auto-deploy infrastructure-related debugs.

params.name: parser
params.description: Enables the logging of the manifest file parsing debugs.

params.name: schedule
params.description: Enables the logging of EEM policy provisioning debugs.

name: default
detail: Set policy provisioning commands to the default state.
syntax: default {enable | exit | log-url | manifest format xml url | retry count retry-count interval interval-duration | schedule start-in hours hours minutes minutes {oneshot | recurring {days days | hours hours}} | window minutes}

params.name: enable
params.description: Enables the profile.

params.name: exit
params.description: Exits auto-deploy configuration mode.

params.name: log-url
params.description: Sets the location where the log file for policy provisioning must be stored.

params.name: manifest format xml url
params.description: Sets the manifest file format, and the location from where the manifest file must be downloaded.

params.name: retry count retry-count interval interval-duration
params.description: Sets the number of retries to transfer a file, if the file transfer is not successful.

params.name: schedule start-in hours hours minutes minutes
params.description: Schedules policy provisioning after the specified time.

params.name: oneshot
params.description: Schedules policy provisioning.

params.name: recurring days days hours hours
params.description: Schedules recurring policy provisioning during the specified time.

params.name: window minutes
params.description: Sets a random time for profile provisioning to be triggered. The window duration is added to the scheduled start-in time, and policy provisioning will happen any time between the scheduled start-in time and the configured window duration.

name: description
detail: Describe an Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) source session.

params.name: description
params.description: Describes the properties for this session.

modes: ERSPAN monitor source session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src)
usageSummary: The description argument can be up to 240 characters.

name: destination
detail: Configure an Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) source session destination and specify destination properties.
modes: ERSPAN monitor source session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src)
usageSummary: ERSPAN traffic is GRE-encapsulated SPAN traffic that can only be processed by an ERSPAN destination session.  All ERSPAN source session (maximum 8) destination IP address need not be same.  Enter the ip address command to configure the IP address for the ERSPAN destination sessions.

name: enable
detail: Enable the Embedded Event Manager (EEM) profile.
syntax: enable This command has no arguments or keywords.
usageSummary: Unless the configured profile is enabled, that profile will not be active, and policy provisioning will not start.

name: erspan-id
detail: Configure the ID used by the destination session to identify the Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) traffic.

params.name: erspan-id
params.description: ERSPAN ID used by the destination session. Valid values are from 1 to 1023.

modes: ERSPAN monitor destination session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src-dst)

name: event manager auto-deploy
detail: Configure an Embedded Event Manager (EEM) auto-deployment profile.
noForm: no event manager auto-deploy name profile-name

params.name: name profile-name
params.description: Specifies a name for the auto-deployment profile.

usageSummary: After you configure this command, the mode changes to auto-deploy configuration mode.  Auto-deployment configuration settings can be configure in this mode.  At any given point of time, more than one profile cannot be enabled.

name: event manager auto-deploy start
detail: Trigger the Embedded Event Manager (EEM) auto-deployment instantly, and to start the policy processing.
syntax: event manager auto-deploy start name profile-name {now | window duration}

params.name: name profile-name
params.description: Specifies a name for the auto-deployment profile.

params.name: now
params.description: Species that the EEM auto-deployment should start immediately.

params.name: window duration
params.description: Specifies that the EEM auto-deployment should start at any random time of the specified window duration. Valid values for the duration argument are 5 to 30 minutes.

name: filter
detail: Configure the Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) source VLAN filtering when the ERSPAN source is a trunk port.
syntax: filter {ip access-group {standard-access-list extended-access-list acl-name} | ipv6 access-group acl-name | mac access-group acl-name | sgt sgt-id [{,}] [{-}] | vlan vlan-id [{,}] [{-}]} [{access-group}] | mac [{access-group}] | sgt sgt-id [{,}] [{-}] | vlan vlan-id [{,}] [{-}]}

params.name: ip
params.description: Specifies the IP access control rules.

params.name: access-group
params.description: Specifies an access control group. standard-access-list Standard IP access list. extended-access-list Extended IP access list.

params.name: acl-name
params.description: Access list name.

params.name: ipv6
params.description: Specifies the IPv6 access control rules.

params.name: mac
params.description: Specifies the media access control (MAC) rules.

params.name: sgt sgt-ID
params.description: Specifies the Security Group Tag (SGT). Valid values are from 1 to 65535.

params.name: vlan vlan-ID
params.description: Specifies the ERSPAN source VLAN. Valid values are from 1 to 4094.
(Optional) Specifies another VLAN.
(Optional) Specifies a range of VLANs.

modes: ERSPAN monitor source session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src)
usageSummary: You cannot include source VLANs and filter VLANs in the same session.  When you configure the filter command on a monitored trunk interface, only traffic on that set of specified VLANs is monitored.

name: header-type
detail: Configure the ERSPAN header type for encapsulation.

params.name: header-type
params.description: ERSPAN header type. Valid header types are 2 and 3.

modes: ERSPAN monitor source session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src)

name: ip dscp
detail: Configure Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) values for packets in the Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) traffic.

params.name: dscp-value
params.description: DSCP value. Valid values are from 0 to 63.

modes: ERSPAN monitor destination session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src-dst)

name: ip ttl
detail: Configure Time to Live (TTL) values for packets in the Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) traffic.

params.name: ttl-value
params.description: TTL value. Valid values are from 2 to 255.

modes: ERSPAN monitor destination session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src-dst)

name: ip wccp
detail: Enable the web cache service, and specify the service number that corresponds to a dynamic service that is defined by the application engine.
syntax: ip wccp {web-cache | service-number} [group-address groupaddress] [group-list access-list] [redirect-list access-list] [password encryption-number password] [redirect-list access-list] [password encryption-number password]
noForm: no ip wccp {web-cache | service-number} [group-address groupaddress] [group-list access-list]

params.name: web-cache
params.description: Specifies the web-cache service (WCCP Version 1 and Version 2).

params.name: service-number
params.description: Dynamic service identifier, which means the service definition is dictated by the cache. The dynamic service number can be from 0 to 254. The maximum number of services is 256, which includes the web-cache service specified with the web-cache keyword.

params.name: group-address groupaddress
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the multicast group address used by the devices and the application engines to participate in the service group.

params.name: group-list access-list
params.description: (Optional) If a multicast group address is not used, specifies a list of valid IP addresses that correspond to the application engines that are participating in the service group.

params.name: redirect-list access-list
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the redirect service for specific hosts or specific packets from hosts.

params.name: password encryption-number
params.description: (Optional) Specifies an encryption number. The range is 0 to 7. Use

params.name: password
params.description: 0 for not encrypted, and use 7 for proprietary. Also, specifies a password name up to seven characters in length. The device combines the password with the MD5 authentication value to create security for the connection between the device and the application engine. By default, no password is configured, and no authentication is performed.

usageSummary: WCCP transparent caching bypasses Network Address Translation (NAT) when Cisco Express Forwarding switching is enabled.  To work around this situation, configure WCCP transparent caching in the outgoing direction, enable Cisco Express Forwarding switching on the content engine interface, and specify the ip wccp web-cache redirect out command.  Configure WCCP in the incoming direction on the inside interface by Command Reference, Cisco IOS XE Gibraltar 16.

name: log-url
detail: Specify the location where provisioning logs must be stored.

params.name: URL
params.description: Location for status logs.

usageSummary: The log URL can be configured either in the manifest file or by using the log-url command.  If the log URL is configured by both ways, the log URL in the manifest file is used.

name: manifest format
detail: Specify the manifest file format and location details.

params.name: xml
params.description: Specifies the manifest file format as XML. url URL Specifies the location to store manifest files.

usageSummary: Valid values for the URL argument are the following: • flash: • ftp: • http: • https: • tftp:

name: map platform-type
detail: Set the parameter map attribute filter criteria to platform type.
syntax: map-number map platform-type {{eq | not-eq | regex} platform-type} map-number Specifies the parameter map number. eq Specifies the filter type name is equal to the platform type name. not-eq Specifies the filter type name is not equal to the platform type name. regex Specifies the filter type name is a regular expression. platform-type Specifies the platform type for the parameter map attribute filter criteria.
noForm: no map-number map platform-type {{eq | not-eq | regex} platform-type}

name: match platform-type
detail: Evaluate control classes based on the platform type.

params.name: platform-name
params.description: Specifies the name of the platform.

name: monitor capture
detail: Configure monitor capture points specifying an attachment point and the packet flow direction or add more attachment points to a capture point.
syntax: monitor capture {capture-name}{interface interface-type interface-id | control-plane}{in | out | both} out | both}
noForm: no monitor capture {capture-name}{interface interface-type interface-id | control-plane}{in |

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be defined.

params.name: interface interface-type interface-id
params.description: Specifies an interface with interface-type and interface-id as an attachment point. The arguments have these meanings:

params.name: control-plane
params.description: Specifies the control plane as an attachment point.

params.name: in | out | both
params.description: Specifies the traffic direction to be captured.

usageSummary: Once an attachment point has been associated with a capture point using this command, the only way to change its direction is to remove the attachment point using the no form of the command and reattach the attachment point with the new direction.  An attachment point's direction cannot be overridden.  If an attachment point is removed from a capture point and only one attachment point is associated with it, the capture point is effectively deleted.

name: monitor capture buffer
detail: Configure the buffer for monitor capture (WireShark).
syntax: monitor capture {capture-name} buffer {circular [size buffer-size ] | size buffer-size}

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture whose buffer is to be configured.

params.name: circular
params.description: Specifies that the buffer is of a circular type. The circular type of buffer continues to capture data, even after the buffer is consumed, by overwriting the data captured previously.

params.name: size buffer-size
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the size of the buffer. The range is from 1 MB to 100 MB.

usageSummary: When you first configure a WireShark capture, a circular buffer of a small size is suggested.

name: monitor capture clear
detail: Clears the monitor capture (WireShark) buffer.

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture whose buffer is to be cleared.

usageSummary: Use the monitor capture clear command either during capture or after the capture has stopped either because one or more end conditions has been met, or you entered the monitor capture stop command.  If you enter the monitor capture clear command after the capture has stopped, the monitor capture export command that is used to store the contents of the captured packets in a file will have no impact because the buffer has no captured packets.  If you have more than one capture that is storing packets in a buffer, clear the buffer before starting a new capture to avoid memory loss.

name: monitor capture export
detail: Export a monitor capture (WireShark) to a file.

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be exported.

params.name: file-location : file-name
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the location and file name of the capture storage file. Acceptable values for file-location : • flash—On-board flash storage • (usbflash0:)— USB drive

usageSummary: Use the monitor capture export command only when the storage destination is a capture buffer.  The file may be stored either remotely or locally.  Use this command either during capture or after the packet capture has stopped.

name: monitor capture file
detail: Configure monitor capture (WireShark) storage file attributes.
syntax: monitor capture {capture-name} file{[ buffer-size temp-buffer-size ][ location file-location : file-name ][ ring number-of-ring-files ][ size total-size ]}
noForm: no monitor capture {capture-name} file{[ buffer-size ][ location ][ ring ][ size ]}

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be modified.

params.name: buffer-size temp-buffer-size
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the size of the temporary buffer. The range for temp-buffer-size is 1 to 100 MB. This is specified to reduce packet loss.

params.name: location file-location : file-name
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the location and file name of the capture storage file. Acceptable values for file-location : • flash—On-board flash storage • (usbflash0:)— USB drive

params.name: ring number-of-ring-files
params.description: (Optional) Specifies that the capture is to be stored in a circular file chain and the number of files in the file ring.

params.name: size total-size
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the total size of the capture files.

usageSummary: Use the monitor capture file command only when the storage destination is a file.  The file may be stored either remotely or locally.  Use this command after the packet capture has stopped.

name: monitor capture limit
detail: Configure capture limits.
syntax: monitor capture {capture-name} limit {[duration seconds][packet-length size][packets num]}

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be assigned capture limits.

params.name: duration seconds
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the duration of the capture, in seconds. The range is from 1 to 1000000.

params.name: packet-length size
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the packet length, in bytes. If the actual packet is longer than the specified length, only the first set of bytes whose number is denoted by the bytes argument is stored.

params.name: packets num
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the number of packets to be processed for capture.

name: monitor capture match
syntax: Note Do not use this command when capturing a CAPWAP tunnel. Also, when control plane and CAPWAP tunnels are mixed, this command will have no effect. To define an explicit inline core filter for a monitor (Wireshark) capture, use the monitor capture match command in privileged EXEC mode. To remove this filter, use the no form of this command. monitor capture {capture-name} match {any | mac mac-match-string | ipv4 {any | host | protocol}{any | host} | ipv6 {any | host | protocol}{any | host}}

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be assigned a core filter.

params.name: any
params.description: Specifies all packets. mac mac-match-string Specifies a Layer 2 packet.

params.name: ipv4
params.description: Specifies IPv4 packets.

params.name: host
params.description: Specifies the host.

params.name: protocol
params.description: Specifies the protocol.

params.name: ipv6
params.description: Specifies IPv6 packets.

name: monitor capture start
detail: Start the capture of packet data at a traffic trace point into a buffer.

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be started.

usageSummary: Use the monitor capture clear command to enable the packet data capture after the capture point is defined.  To stop the capture of packet data, use the monitor capture stop command.  Ensure that system resources such as CPU and memory are available before starting a capture.

name: monitor capture stop
detail: Stop the capture of packet data at a traffic trace point.

params.name: capture-name
params.description: The name of the capture to be stopped.

usageSummary: Use the monitor capture stop command to stop the capture of packet data that you started using the monitor capture start command.  You can configure two types of capture buffers: linear and circular.  When the linear buffer is full, data capture stops automatically.

name: monitor session
detail: Create a new Ethernet Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) or a Remote Switched Port Analyzer (RSPAN) or Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) session configuration for analyzing traffic between ports or add to an existing session configuration.
syntax: monitor session session-number {destination | filter | source | type {erspan-destination | erspan-source}} | erspan-source}] | all | local | range session-range | remote}
noForm: no monitor session {session-number [destination | filter | source | type {erspan-destination

params.name: session-number
params.description: The session number identified with the sessio

params.name: all
params.description: Clears all monitor sessions.

params.name: local
params.description: Clears all local monitor sessions.

params.name: range session-range
params.description: Clears monitor sessions in the specified range

params.name: remote
params.description: Clears all remote monitor sessions.

usageSummary: You can set a combined maximum of two local SPAN sessions and RSPAN source sessions.  You can have a total of 66 SPAN, RSPAN, and ERSPAN sessions on a switch or switch stack.  You can verify your settings by entering the show monitor privileged EXEC command.

name: monitor session destination
detail: Start a new Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) session or Remote SPAN (RSPAN) destination session, to enable ingress traffic on the destination port for a network security device (such as a Cisco IDS Sensor Appliance), and to add or delete interfaces or VLANs to or from an existing SPAN or RSPAN session.
syntax: monitor session session-number destination {interface interface-id [, | -] [encapsulation {replicate | dot1q} ] {ingress [dot1q | untagged] } | {remote} vlan vlan-id {replicate | dot1q} ] {ingress [dot1q | untagged] } | {remote} vlan vlan-id
noForm: no monitor session session-number destination {interface interface-id [, | -] [encapsulation

params.name: session-number
params.description: The session number identified with the SPAN

params.name: interface interface-id
params.description: Specifies the destination or source interface fo physical ports (including type, stack member, channel is also a valid interface type, and the
(Optional) Specifies a series of interfaces or V from a previous range. Enter a space before a
(Optional) Specifies a range of interfaces or V

params.name: encapsulation replicate
params.description: (Optional) Specifies that the destination interfa If not selected, the default is to send packets i These keywords are valid only for local SPAN original VLAN ID; therefore, packets are alw ignored with the no form of the command.

params.name: encapsulation dot1q
params.description: (Optional) Specifies that the destination interf IEEE 802.1Q encapsulation. These keywords are valid only for local SPAN original VLAN ID; therefore, packets are alw ignored with the no form of the command.

params.name: ingress

params.name: dot1q
params.description: (Optional) Accepts incoming packets with IE the default VLAN.

params.name: untagged
params.description: (Optional) Accepts incoming packets with un default VLAN.

params.name: isl

params.name: remote
params.description: Specifies the remote VLAN for an RSPAN so 1006 to 4094. The RSPAN VLAN cannot be VLAN 1 (the d for Token Ring and FDDI VLANs).

params.description: Sets the default VLAN for ingress traffic w

usageSummary: You can set a combined maximum of 8 local SPAN sessions and RSPAN source sessions.  You can have a total of 66 SPAN and RSPAN sessions on a switch or switch stack.  A SPAN or RSPAN destination must be a physical port.

name: monitor session filter
detail: Start a new flow-based SPAN (FSPAN) session or flow-based RSPAN (FRSPAN) source or destination session, or to limit (filter) SPAN source traffic to specific VLANs.
noForm: no monitor session session-number filter {vlan vlan-id [, | -] }

params.name: session-number
params.description: The session number identified with the SPAN or RSPAN ses

params.name: vlan vlan-id
params.description: Specifies a list of VLANs as filters on trunk source ports to lim VLANs. The vlan-id range is 1 to 4094.
(Optional) Specifies a series of VLANs, or separates a range Enter a space before and after the comma.
(Optional) Specifies a range of VLANs. Enter a space before

usageSummary: You can set a combined maximum of two local SPAN sessions and RSPAN source sessions.  You can have a total of 66 SPAN and RSPAN sessions on a switch or switch stack.  You can monitor traffic on a single VLAN or on a series or range of ports or VLANs.

name: monitor session source
detail: Start a new Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) session or Remote SPAN (RSPAN) source session, or to add or delete interfaces or VLANs to or from an existing SPAN or RSPAN session.
syntax: monitor session session_number source {interface interface-id [, | -] [both | rx | tx] | [remote] vlan vlan-id [, | -] [both | rx | tx]} [remote] vlan vlan-id [, | -] [both | rx | tx]}
noForm: no monitor session session_number source {interface interface-id [, | -] [both | rx | tx] |

params.name: session_number
params.description: The session number identified with the SPAN or RSPAN session. The range is 1 to 66.

params.name: interface interface-id
params.description: Specifies the source interface for a SPAN or RSPAN session. Valid interfaces are physical ports (including type, stack member, module, and port number). For source interface, port channel is also a valid interface type, and the valid range is 1 to 48.
(Optional) Specifies a series of interfaces or VLANs, or separates a range of interfaces or VLANs from a previous range. Enter a space before and after the comma.
(Optional) Specifies a range of interfaces or VLANs. Enter a space before and after the hyphen.

params.name: both | rx | tx
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the traffic direction to monitor. If you do not specify a traffic direction, the source interface sends both transmitted and received traffic.

params.name: remote
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the remote VLAN for an RSPAN source or destination session. The range is 2 to 1001 and 1006 to 4094. The RSPAN VLAN cannot be VLAN 1 (the default VLAN) or VLAN IDs 1002 to 1005 (reserved for Token Ring and FDDI VLANs).

params.name: vlan vlan-id
params.description: When used with only the ingress keyword, sets default VLAN for ingress traffic.

usageSummary: Traffic that enters or leaves source ports or source VLANs can be monitored by using SPAN or RSPAN.  Traffic routed to source ports or source VLANs cannot be monitored.  You can set a combined maximum of two local SPAN sessions and RSPAN source sessions.

name: monitor session type
detail: Configure a local Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) session.
noForm: no monitor session span-session-number type {erspan-destination | erspan-source}

params.name: span-session-number
params.description: Number of the local ERSPAN session. Valid values are from 1 to 66.

usageSummary: The span-session-number and the session type cannot be changed once configured.  Use the no form of this command to remove the session and then re-create the session with a new session ID or a new session type.  The ERSPAN source session destination IP address, which must be configured on an interface on the destination switch, is the source of traffic that an ERSPAN destination session sends to the destination ports.

name: mtu
detail: Configure the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size for ERSPAN truncation.

params.name: bytes
params.description: MTU size, in bytes. The default value of MTU is 9000 bytes.

modes: ERSPAN monitor destination session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src-dst)

name: origin
detail: Configure the IP address used as the source of the Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) traffic.

params.name: ip-address
params.description: Specifies the ERSPAN source session destination IP address.

modes: ERSPAN monitor destination session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src-dst)
usageSummary: ERSPAN source session on a switch can use different source IP addresses using the origin command.

name: retry count
detail: Set the number of retries to transfer a file, if the file transfer is not successful.
noForm: no retry count retry-count interval interval-duration

params.name: retry-count
params.description: Number of retries to transfer a file, if file transfer is not successful. Valid values are from 1 to 3.

params.name: interval interval-duration
params.description: Specifies the interval between retries. Valid values are from 2 to 4 minutes.

name: schedule start-in
detail: Schedule the provisioning of policies.
syntax: schedule start-in hours hours minutes minutes {oneshot | recurring {days days | hours hours}}
noForm: no schedule start-in hours hours minutes minutes {oneshot | recurring {days days | hours hours}}

params.name: hours hours
params.description: Specifies the time in hours, when the policy provisioning should start. Valid values are from 0 to 23.

params.name: minutes minutes
params.description: Specifies the time in minutes, when the policy provisioning should start. Valid values are from 0 to 59.

params.name: oneshot
params.description: Schedules the policy provisioning to be done only once.

params.name: recurring
params.description: Schedules the policy provisioning repeatedly.

params.name: days days
params.description: Specifies the time in days, when the policy provisioning should repeat. Valid values are from 1 to 30.

params.name: hours hours
params.description: Specifies the time in hours, when the policy provisioning should repeat. Valid values are from 12 to 168.

name: show capability feature monitor
detail: Display information about monitor features.

params.name: erspan-destination
params.description: Displays information about the configured Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) source sessions.

params.name: erspan-source
params.description: Displays all the configured global built-in templates.

name: show class-map type control subscriber
detail: Display class map statistics for the configured control policies.
syntax: show class-map type control subscriber {all|name control-class-name}

params.name: all
params.description: Displays class map statistics for all control policies.

params.name: name control-class-name
params.description: Displays class map statistics for the specified control policy.

name: show event manager auto-deploy summary
detail: Display a summary of the auto-deployment profile information.
syntax: show event manager auto-deploy summary This command has no arguments or keywords.

name: show ip sla statistics
detail: Display current or aggregated operational status and statistics of all Cisco IOS IP Service Level Agreement (SLA) operations or a specified operation.
syntax: show ip sla statistics [ operation-number [details] | aggregated [ operation-number | details] | details]

params.name: operation-number
params.description: (Optional) Number of the operation for which operational status and statistics are displayed. Accepted values are from 1 to 2147483647.

params.name: details
params.description: (Optional) Specifies detailed output.

params.name: aggregated
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the IP SLA aggregated statistics.

usageSummary: Use the show ip sla statistics to display the current state of IP SLA operations, including how much life the operation has left, whether the operation is active, and the completion time.  The output also includes the monitoring data returned for the last (most recently completed) operation.  This generated operation ID is displayed when you use the show ip sla configuration command for the base multicast operation, and as part of the summary statistics for the entire operation.

name: show monitor
detail: Display information about all Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) and Remote SPAN (RSPAN) sessions.
syntax: show monitor [session {session_number | all | local | range list | remote} [detail]]

params.name: session
params.description: (Optional) Displays information about specified SPAN sessions.

params.name: session_number
params.description: The session number identified with the SPAN or RSPAN session. The range is 1 to 66.

params.name: all
params.description: (Optional) Displays all SPAN sessions.

params.name: local
params.description: (Optional) Displays only local SPAN sessions.

params.name: range list
params.description: (Optional) Displays a range of SPAN sessions, where list is the range of valid sessions. The range is either a single session or a range of sessions described by two numbers, the lower one first, separated by a hyphen. Do not enter any spaces between comma-separated parameters or in hyphen-specified ranges. Note This keyword is available only in privileged EXEC mode.

params.name: remote
params.description: (Optional) Displays only remote SPAN sessions.

params.name: detail
params.description: (Optional) Displays detailed information about the specified sessions.

usageSummary: The output is the same for the show monitor command and the show monitor session all command.

name: show monitor capture
detail: Display monitor capture (WireShark) content.
syntax: show monitor capture [capture-name [ buffer ] | file file-location : file-name ][ brief | detailed | display-filter display-filter-string ]

params.name: capture-name
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the name of the capture to be displayed.

name: snmp-server host
detail: Specify the recipient (host) of a Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) notification operation.
syntax: snmp-server host {host-addr } [vrf vrf-instance ] [informs | traps] [version {1 | 2c | 3 {auth | noauth | priv} } ] {community-string [notification-type] } 3 {auth | noauth | priv} } ] {community-string [notification-type] }

params.name: host-addr
params.description: Name or Internet address of the host (the targeted recipient).

params.name: vrf vrf-instance
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the virtual private network (VPN) routing instance and name for this host.

params.name: informs | traps
params.description: (Optional) Sends SNMP traps or informs to this host.

params.name: version 1 | 2c |
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the version of the SNMP used to send the traps. 3 1—SNMPv1. This option is not available with informs. 2c—SNMPv2C. 3—SNMPv3. One of the authorization keywords (see next table row) must follow the Version 3 keyword.

params.name: auth | noauth auth
params.description: (Optional)—Enables Message Digest 5 (MD5) and Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA)

params.name: | priv
params.description: packet authentication. noauth (Default)—The noAuthNoPriv security level. This is the default if the auth | noauth | priv keyword choice is not specified. priv (Optional)—Enables Data Encryption Standard (DES) packet encryption (also called privacy).

params.name: community-string
params.description: Password-like community string sent with the notification operation. Though you can set this string by using the snmp-server host command, we recommend that you define this string by using the snmp-server community global configuration command before using the snmp-server host command. Note The @ symbol is used for delimiting the context information. Avoid using the @ symbol as part of the SNMP community string when configuring this command. notification-type (Optional) Type of notification to be sent to the host. If no type is specified, all notifications are sent. The notification type can be one or more of the these keywords: • auth-framework—Sends SNMP CISCO-AUTH-FRAMEWORK-MIB traps. • bridge—Sends SNMP Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) bridge MIB traps. • bulkstat—Sends Data-Collection-MIB Collection notification traps. • call-home—Sends SNMP CISCO-CALLHOME-MIB traps. • cef—Sends SNMP CEF traps. • config—Sends SNMP configuration traps. • config-copy—Sends SNMP config-copy traps. • config-ctid—Sends SNMP config-ctid traps. • copy-config—Sends SNMP copy configuration traps. • cpu—Sends CPU notification traps. • cpu threshold—Sends CPU threshold notification traps. • eigrp—Sends SNMP EIGRP traps. • entity—Sends SNMP entity traps. • envmon—Sends environmental monitor traps. • errdisable—Sends SNMP errdisable notification traps. • event-manager—Sends SNMP Embedded Event Manager traps. • flash—Sends SNMP FLASH notifications. • flowmon—Sends SNMP flowmon notification traps. • ipmulticast—Sends SNMP IP multicast routing traps. • ipsla—Sends SNMP IP SLA traps. • isis—Sends IS-IS traps. • license—Sends license traps. • local-auth—Sends SNMP local auth traps. • mac-notification—Sends SNMP MAC notification traps. • ospf—Sends Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) traps. • pim—Sends SNMP Protocol-Independent Multicast (PIM) traps. • port-security—Sends SNMP port-security traps. • power-ethernet—Sends SNMP power Ethernet traps. • snmp—Sends SNMP-type traps. • storm-control—Sends SNMP storm-control traps. • stpx—Sends SNMP STP extended MIB traps. • syslog—Sends SNMP syslog traps. • transceiver—Sends SNMP transceiver traps. • tty—Sends TCP connection traps. • vlan-membership— Sends SNMP VLAN membership traps. • vlancreate—Sends SNMP VLAN-created traps. • vlandelete—Sends SNMP VLAN-deleted traps. • vrfmib—Sends SNMP vrfmib traps. • vstack—Sends SNMP Smart Install traps. • vtp—Sends SNMP VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP) traps.

usageSummary: SNMP notifications can be sent as traps or inform requests.  Traps are unreliable because the receiver does not send acknowledgments when it receives traps.  The sender cannot determine if the traps were received.

name: source
detail: Configure the Encapsulated Remote Switched Port Analyzer (ERSPAN) source interface or VLAN, and the traffic direction to be monitored.
syntax: source {interface type number | vlan vlan-ID}[{, | - | both | rx | tx}]

params.name: interface type number
params.description: Specifies an interface type and number.

params.name: vlan vlan-ID
params.description: Associates the ERSPAN source session number with VLANs. Valid values are from 1 to 4094.
(Optional) Specifies another interface.
(Optional) Specifies a range of interfaces.

params.name: both
params.description: (Optional) Monitors both received and transmitted ERSPAN traffic.

params.name: rx
params.description: (Optional) Monitors only received traffic.

params.name: tx
params.description: (Optional) Monitors only transmitted traffic.

modes: ERSPAN monitor source session configuration mode (config-mon-erspan-src)
usageSummary: You cannot include source VLANs and filter VLANs in the same session.

name: status syslog
detail: Send the status of provisioning policies to the syslog.
syntax: status syslog This command has no arguments or keywords.

name: switchport mode access
detail: Sets the interface as a nontrunking nontagged single-VLAN Ethernet interface.

name: switchport voice vlan
detail: Specify to forward all voice traffic through the specified VLAN.

params.name: vlan_id
params.description: Specifies to forward all voice traffic through the specified VLAN.

name: window
detail: Set a random time for profile provisioning to be triggered.

params.name: minutes
params.description: Time in minutes. Valid values are from 1 to 60.

usageSummary: The window duration is added to the time configured by the schedule start-in command.  Profile provisioning is triggered at random time between the specified schedule and the configured window duration.
